notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.51_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.51.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.51.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.
**VPS** — `ruzed-0.0.51-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (or `-aarch64`) is the daemon a server can be hosted on, for a Linux machine you run. The README inside says how to set it up. On a Windows machine, run `ruzed-0.0.51-windows-x86_64-setup.exe`, which installs it as a service.

---

*A window each* becomes a whole way to use Ruze: the friends list is the app,
and every channel and call opens in a window of its own. A shared screen can
be smooth enough for games and video, a camera that will not start no longer
gets stuck, the tray icon matches the icons around it, and Exit no longer
freezes on the way out.

### Added

- **Share a screen at 30 or 60 frames a second.** Settings → Video quality
  has a *Shared screen frame rate*, and it is one or the other: a shared
  screen no longer drops to 15, 10 or 5 frames a second at its lower
  qualities. Every quality is 30 fps, and 60 is there for games and video.
  More frames cost more upload, so on a slower connection the screen is sent
  smaller rather than choppier. Changing it while you are sharing applies
  straight away.

- **Host servers on a Windows machine.** ruzed, the VPS a server can be bound
  to, now runs on Windows as well as Linux, with an installer of its own:
  `ruzed-0.0.51-windows-x86_64-setup.exe`. It asks for the name members reach
  the machine by, sets ruzed up as a service that starts with Windows, opens
  it in the firewall, and offers to mint a host code at the end. A machine
  at home works too, with a port forward on the router.

- **The friends list is the whole app in *A window each*.** With that
  layout chosen in Settings → Layout, the main window no longer opens.
  Clicking the tray icon, or launching Ruze again, brings up the friends
  list. Its title bar has the connection dot and a settings button. Servers
  are made or joined from the ＋ beside *Servers*, and right-clicking a
  server offers invites, server settings and leaving it. Friend requests,
  device pairing, people asking to join your server and new versions all
  show up there too.

- **A window for every channel and call.** In *A window each*, the servers
  at the foot of the friends list open out to their channels and live
  channels, one server at a time. A text channel opens in a window of its
  own; a live channel opens in its own window to look in, and the phone
  beside it joins. The microphone beside a server starts a live chat there.
  Close a call's window and you stay in the call: the friends list shows
  it, with mute, hang up, and the way back to its window. Your camera and
  shared screen go off with the window, since that is what was showing
  them. A reply you are already reading in a channel's window no longer
  raises a system notification.

- **See who is about at a glance.** Everyone in a live channel is listed
  under it by name, as in the main window, and clicking a name gives their
  volume and profile. A dot on a folded server says how many people are live
  in it, and the faces beside its name say who in it is online — point at
  them for everyone by name, with whether they are away or busy.

- **A tidier friends list.** Friends are one list again — whoever is online
  first, then everyone else — with an *online* filter at the right of its
  heading for when only they matter. Friends and servers share one heading
  style, each folds away and stays folded, and either can be moved above the
  other. Search is a magnifier in the bar that slides a search field out,
  instead of a box always taking up a row.

### Changed

- **Links and pictures take up less of the conversation.** A link's
  preview, and a picture, video or GIF posted in a channel, is a good deal
  smaller: about a third of the window's height at most, and well under
  half its width. A
  YouTube Short gets narrower to keep its shape, a long post scrolls inside
  its card, and clicking a picture or pressing *Open* still shows the full
  thing.

- **The tray icon is monochrome.** The teal mask in the tray is now drawn
  the way the icons around it are: white with a solid dark grey shadow on a
  dark taskbar, black and grey on a light one. On Windows it follows the
  taskbar's own light or dark setting, and switches when that does. When
  you are away the shadowed side fades back. The setting that drew the tray
  icon in your accent colour is gone, since there is no colour left to
  change.

- **Settings on a phone or in a narrow window is a list you can read.** The
  sections used to be a row of buttons that ran off the edge of the screen.
  Now they are a list, each with a line saying what is in it. Tapping one
  opens it, and *‹ Settings* at the top goes back. Searching shows only the
  sections that match.

### Fixed

- **A channel says it is loading, not that it is empty.** Opening a text
  channel said *No messages yet* until its history arrived a moment later.
  It now says it is loading until it has.

- **Exit no longer freezes on the way out.** Choosing *Exit Ruze* left every
  window on screen, not responding, while Ruze said goodbye to each peer —
  for as long as the slowest of them took to answer. Now the windows and the
  tray icon go at once, and the goodbyes happen out of sight, for a few
  seconds at most.

- **Leaving a live channel takes you out of it everywhere.** Leaving from
  the live channel's own window left the friends list showing you still in
  it, and still showing the channel after it had ended because you were the
  last one there.

- **Muting shows as muted everywhere.** Muting in one window left every other
  window showing your microphone on.

- **A camera that will not start at one size is tried at smaller ones.** A
  webcam that lit up, went dark and failed with *Could not start video
  source* at the size the video quality asked for used to end there. Ruze now
  tries the next size down, and then the camera's own default, before giving
  up, and the message says what to try. A camera in a call also keeps the size
  it started at, rather than being asked to switch as people join and leave,
  which some webcams handle badly.

- **The camera can be turned on again after it fails.** A camera that
  stopped the moment it started left Ruze thinking it was still on, and the
  camera button did nothing until Ruze was restarted.

- **Settings no longer leaves your camera on.** Closing settings while its
  camera preview was still opening left the camera running, light and all,
  until Ruze was closed.

- **Joining from your desktop offers to take the call back from your
  phone.** After moving a call to your phone, joining the same room from your
  desktop went straight in, instead of asking whether to move the call back or
  join on both. The desktop could not see your phone in the room. It only
  believed a device that had its own entry in the server, and a newly linked
  phone may not have one yet. A device now counts when its account is in the
  server, which the account vouches for with its own signature. Somebody
  removed from a server stays out, on every device.

- **A shared screen sends the frame rate it promises.** Frames that arrived a
  little early were dropped, so a screen set to 15 frames a second went out at
  about 10. It now holds the rate it was set to.
